transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi. Well, honestly, the thing that scared me into coming in is that my eating has just been all over the place lately. Like, some days I completely forget to eat meals at all, and then... other nights I'm just tearing through takeout and a bunch of snacks way after midnight. It's just really off right now.
Have you noticed any change in your weight recently?

I haven't actually stepped on a scale recently, but it's probably fluctuating. Like I was just saying, my appetite is completely unpredictable right now. Going from forgetting to eat entirely to just gorging on takeout and snacks at two in the morning... that extreme shift is really what scared me into making this appointment. So I imagine my weight is bouncing around right along with it.
Do you find that your eating is triggered by how you're feeling, such as when you're stressed or anxious?

I'm not really sure if it's tied to stress or anything like that. I haven't really noticed a pattern with my mood triggering it. It just sort of happens... I either don't think about food at all, or I can't stop eating. I haven't really connected it to feeling anxious or anything.
Do you often feel guilty after eating, especially after those late-night episodes of consuming a lot of food?

Not really, no. I mean, I don't sit there beating myself up over the calories or feeling bad about myself after it happens. It's more just... I guess I just realize it's weird that my appetite is doing this out of nowhere. But I wouldn't say I feel guilty after I eat.
Are you afraid of gaining weight?

No, not really. I mean, I guess I wouldn't be thrilled to put on a bunch of weight, but it's not something I'm actively afraid of or stressing over. I haven't really been thinking about the number on the scale. I'm just more concerned about why my eating habits are suddenly so out of whack.
Do you ever feel like you're losing control while you're eating?

No, I wouldn't say I feel out of control. It's more like I just get really hungry and I eat. I'm not, like, frantically stuffing my face or feeling like I can't stop myself. It's just that I end up eating a lot more than usual before I feel full. But I still feel like I'm the one deciding to eat.
Are there times when you just don't feel like eating at all, not because you're not hungry, but because food doesn't sound appealing to you?

No, not really. Food usually sounds fine to me. I don't think I've had times where... where I just don't want to eat because nothing sounds good. If I'm hungry, I eat. It's really just been the opposite lately, where I'm just eating a lot more than normal.
Do you find that there are times when you're just not interested in eating because you're not feeling hungry?

Honestly, yeah. That's actually the main thing that scared me into coming in. My eating has just been totally all over the place. Like, some days I'll just forget meals completely because I'm just not hungry or thinking about it. But then other nights I'm just tearing through takeout and snacks after midnight. It's just really back and forth right now.
Do you find yourself losing interest in activities you used to enjoy?

Yeah, actually. I used to do a lot of things... like, I'd play soccer on the weekends, I liked cooking for my girlfriend, I'd go check out these small art galleries around town. I even used to stick around at work to help out the newer sales guys. But lately... I don't know, I just can't make myself care about any of it anymore. It just feels like too much effort for nothing.
Have you been feeling sad or down most of the time lately?

No, not really. I wouldn't say I've been feeling sad or down. It's more just... I don't know, a lack of energy or interest, like I mentioned. But I don't feel like crying or anything like that. I'm just kind of going through the motions right now.
How long have you felt like you can't make yourself care about the things you used to enjoy?

I'd say it's been about four months. The not caring about things, the guilt, and I guess just that overall low feeling... it's been around for about that long. It really got a lot harder to just ignore after I had some trouble at work.
Do you feel like you're depressed most of the time?

I don't know if I'd use the word depressed. I mean... like I said, I don't really feel sad. It's just more of that flat, empty feeling most of the time. I'm not sitting around crying or anything, I just... I just don't have the drive I used to.
Do you feel like you're depressed most of the time, even if it's just a feeling of being empty or flat?

I guess... if that's what you mean by depressed, just being empty, then yeah. That flat feeling is there pretty much all the time. I just don't really know if I'd use that word for it myself, but the emptiness doesn't really go away.
How long have you felt like you can't make yourself care about the things you used to enjoy?
Like I mentioned a minute ago, it's been about four months. That's how long I've had that issue with just not caring about the stuff I normally like doing.
Would you say that this flat, empty feeling you've been experiencing is mild, or is it significantly impacting your daily life?

I'd say it's definitely having a significant impact. My manager has actually started pulling me off some of my accounts because... well, I'm making mistakes that I normally wouldn't make. HR even got involved recently after an employee-assistance call. I mean, I'm still showing up every day, but both work and home just feel like they're slipping out of my control.
Would you describe your flat, empty feeling as something that you can still manage to cope with most days or is it overwhelming most of the time?

I guess I can still manage to cope with it most days. It's not really overwhelming... just, like I said, it's there. I'm still getting up and going to work, even if things are slipping a bit. So, yeah, I can cope with it, it's just frustrating.
Would you say that most days are pretty difficult for you to get through because of this flat, empty feeling?

No, I wouldn't really call it difficult to get through the day. I mean, I'm still doing what I need to do. It's not like a huge struggle to finish out my shift or anything like that. It's just... I'm kind of going through the motions. So, no, not difficult, just empty.
Would you say that this empty feeling is affecting your ability to function at work or in your personal life most of the time?

Yeah, I'd say it is affecting my ability to function most of the time. Like I mentioned earlier, my manager is actually taking me off some of my accounts. I'm just making these mistakes that I wouldn't usually make. And HR even had to step in after that employee-assistance call. I'm still physically showing up to work, but honestly, both my job and my personal life just feel like they're slipping out of my control.
Would you say this empty feeling is more than half the day, most days?
Yeah, I guess so. It's pretty much there all day, most days. I wake up with it, and it just kind of hangs around while I'm at work and when I get home. So, yeah, definitely more than half the day.
